subject.title: [Reliability]: Enforce atomic intent→execution flow to prevent orphan pre-action notices

question: Should OpenClaw define this commit-or-abort guarantee as part of a broader structured process-events contract, or as a separate agent-run transaction API?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the durable fix chooses public lifecycle semantics across protocol, runtime, sessions, clients, and possibly policy/config, so automation cannot safely choose the contract shape.

options.title: Unify With Process Events
options.body: Make begin, execution evidence, commit, abort, and blocker semantics acceptance criteria for one structured process/events contract so clients have a single source of lifecycle truth.

options.title: Create Separate Run Transaction API
options.body: Add a distinct run.begin/run.exec/run.commit/run.abort contract and document how it composes with current lifecycle, item, plan, tool, and process streams.

options.title: Keep Existing Safeguards Only
options.body: Treat strict-agentic retries, liveness states, and no-fake-progress coverage as sufficient, then narrow this issue to documentation or telemetry follow-up.

recommendation.title: Unify With Process Events
recommendation.body: Make begin, execution evidence, commit, abort, and blocker semantics acceptance criteria for one structured process/events contract so clients have a single source of lifecycle truth.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the prior product-contract review and has the strongest owner/history signal for adjacent terminal outcome and agent.wait surfaces.
